behel: Belgium's newest weather radar stands in Houthalen-Helchteren in Limburg and belongs to the Flanders Environment Agency (VMM), not the national weather service. Its dual-polarisation data help separate rain from hail and feed the Flemish rainfall maps used for flood forecasting.
bejab: The Royal Meteorological Institute's coastal radar sits on a 46 m concrete tower in Jabbeke, West Flanders, and was inaugurated in September 2012. It watches showers coming in from the North Sea, where offshore wind farms and ship traffic are a constant source of clutter.
bewid: Belgium's first weather radar has stood on a 50 m guyed steel tower on an Ardennes plateau at Wideumont since 2001, 585 m above sea level with a clear view in every direction. The original single-polarisation radar was replaced by a dual-polarisation one in spring 2022.
